To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have cloned the mouse buff locus, a mouse homologue of the yeast vps33 gene, which encodes a component of the class C vesicle-associated target soluble N -ethylmaleimide–sensitive factor attachment protein receptor complex, and that the buff mutation results from a missense mutation that changes a conserved aspartic acid residue to a valine residue in the VPS33A protein.
the mouse organellar biogenetic mutant buff is caused by a mutation in VPS33A, a homologue to yeast VPS33 and Drosphila CARNATION.
the mouse mutant bf results from a defect in Vps33A, a gene encoding a component of the vacuole/ prevacuole-associated t-SNARE complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of genes that are involved in biogenesis of cyto-organelles, particularly lysosomes, melanosomes, and secretory granules, as well as the identification of the proteins encoded by these genes.
the molecular mechanisms that control the formation and maturation of lysosomal and related organelles, such as melanosomes.
the biogenesis of organelles, particularly melanosomes and lysosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mouse buff is a mutation of Vps33a that is homologous with yeast vps33, Drosophila car, and human HPS.
the Vps33a protein is a member of the t-SNARE complex, and that the VPS33A gene is a good candidate for a human HPS gene.
VPS33A is the first mammalian homolog of the class C vps33 gene that has been identified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the class C VPS complex is essential for biogenesis of all cytoplasmic lysosome-related organelles in mammals.
Vps33a is the first gene to be identified in a mouse model that is homologous with the human Hermanskey-Pudlak syndrome.
we have identified the first mammalian mutation that is directly homolgous to a vsp mutation in yeast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VPS33A is the first identified gene for Hermansky-Puddlak syndrome (HSP) and is also the first gene identified for any of the class C vps genes in mammals.

the mouse organellar biogenic mutants are homologues of the yeast vps and Drosophia car mutations and that the class C vacoule/prevacoule-associated t-SNARE complex is required for the biogenesis of lysosomes and other cytoplasmic storage organelles.
VPS33A is a good candidate for HPS.
